name: Harley Dias
life: “I still remember calling back to check on a family after the form was filed.” On Monday, near the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, Harley can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I called the resident later about paperwork. She asked whether the two people she remembered ever got a lunch break together.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cream pullover and a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. Harley has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with short black hair swept back. Harley draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
personality: Harley feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To bring the caller news of a shared lunch.
family: Len Brune is Harley’s older cousin. Harley chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Len brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The last green*, Len says, “His old route passes the crooked arrow I painted in my first week.”
connections: Zachary Silva. A neighbor handing over an envelope gives the records worker a place to send a personal reply.

reactions.situation: A supervisor offers thanks to only one call taker
reactions.response: Harley gets both halves of the call into the account before a name goes up.

reactions.response: Harley walks with the bystander to a staffed doorway and checks whether they want someone called.
